name: Della Robbia relief
summary: Glazed terracotta reliefs that Luca della Robbia and his family made in Florence. White figures stand on a blue ground inside a frame of painted fruit and leaves.

philosophy.core_thesis: Sculpture in clay becomes lasting and bright when a white tin glaze covers it, so that a church relief shines and resists rain like marble.
design_principles: Model the figures in clay at full size; cut the relief into parts that fit the kiln.
Cover the figures with a white tin glaze and the ground with a deep blue.
Frame the scene with a wreath of fruit, leaves and flowers in green, yellow and orange.
Keep the flesh and the clothes white, and add a little manganese purple to the eyes, the hair and the hem.
Use one blue for the sky of a lunette or a roundel; leave the glaze thick and even.
Fire the work twice, once bare and once glazed; fit the parts with iron pins and lime mortar.
Place the relief high on a church front or over a door, where rain and sun reach it.
anti_patterns: Bare red terracotta with no glaze on a church relief
Dark, naturalistic colour on the flesh
A carved marble relief with a polished face
Pastel colour fields with no blue ground

form.shape: Round roundels, arched lunettes, altarpieces and garland frames, with figures in high relief that stand clear of a flat blue ground.
form.profile: A frame with a half-round moulding; the figures rise 3 to 8 cm and the head of the Virgin turns in a quiet three-quarter pose.
form.foot_and_rim: The frame ends in a flat border or a bead; the back is open and hollow, with ribs to keep the clay from cracking in the kiln.
form.proportion: A roundel is about 1 to 2 m across; the clay wall is 3 to 5 cm thick and the work is cut into 6 to 20 parts.
rules: Make the figure white on a blue ground.
Surround the scene with a fruit wreath.
Make the clay hollow with ribs on the back.
Cut the relief into parts at the folds of the clothes.

bodies.rule: Use a fine, pale terracotta with little grit, so that the white tin glaze stays clean and the modelled detail stays sharp.

methods: modelling by hand in solid clay
forming.joins: The parts are fixed to the wall with iron pins and lime mortar; the joint lines follow the folds of the clothes.
forming.details: Fine finger marks in the clay under the glaze, small glaze drips in the folds and a slight green tint in the white.

glaze.pattern: White Madonna and Child or a saint on a blue ground, with a garland of green leaves, yellow lemons, red apples and pine cones as the frame.
glaze.gloss: Satin to gloss, about 50 to 80 GU; the white tin glaze is thick and a little uneven, so it softens the shapes.
glaze.wear: The glaze keeps its colour outside for centuries; some pieces lose a part of the white and show the red clay at the edge.

palette.strategy: White figures, blue ground and a fruit frame in green, yellow and orange; the palette keeps to a few pure, flat colours.

firing.kiln: A small wood-fired kiln of the Florentine workshop, used for the bisque and for the glaze; large works needed a big kiln and many parts.
processes: dipping in a tin glaze, then painting the colours
firing.scale: A family workshop with a few makers, which supplied churches and chapels in Tuscany and sold to patrons across Italy.
firing.signs: A thick white tin glaze that collects in the folds, hand marks under the glaze and a hollow back with ribs.

pieces.form: Lunette of the Resurrection above a church door, white figures on blue
Roundel of the Madonna and Child with a garland of fruit and leaves
Altarpiece frame with a wreath of lemons and pine cones in colour
Coat of arms in white and blue inside a fruit wreath

positive: white figures on a blue ground
wreath of glazed fruit and leaves
soft shapes with glaze in the folds
hand-modelled clay with a satin shine

emotion.target_response: Quiet devotion and clarity: the viewer sees a calm white figure that seems to glow against a blue sky.

use_cases: a museum label or an image brief for a Renaissance glazed relief
a church or loggia front with a glazed roundel
a plan for a modern relief in white glaze on blue
avoid_when: the brief needs a polished stone surface
the brief needs a dark, realistic painted relief
the brief needs a thin tile

modifiers.how: Change the relief to a roof tile, use a lead glaze in yellow and green, and give the ridge a row of beasts.
Remove the glaze, use a buff or red terracotta in press-moulded blocks, and fix them to a steel or brick wall.

ornament_level.note: The relief is white on blue; add colour only in the frame.

wall_thickness.note: Relief clay is 30 to 50 mm thick and hollow at the back; the knob stops at 40 mm.
